$comment: Injection grammar: HTML inside FAST's html`` templates and CSS inside css``, written for this extension (not vendored from vscode-lit-html — task P5-01 chose write-our-own to avoid carrying a fork of another grammar). This half only opens the template and hands the body over; everything that has to keep working *inside* the body — ${…} and FAST's :/?/@ binding prefixes — lives in `fast-element-embedded.injection.json`, because the first four selectors' `-string` switches the whole grammar off the moment the template's own `string.template.fast-element.ts` scope is on the stack. The fifth selector buys back the one place that `-string` should not have taken away: a template nested in an interpolation of another one, which `when(…, html`…`)` and `repeat(…, html`…`)` write every day. It cannot be a pattern on the opening rule — by the time the inner `html` is reached the stack is inside whatever anonymous rule source.ts pushed for the enclosing argument list, and a rule listed on an ancestor is never consulted again — so it has to be an injection too. The negations name TypeScript's own string scopes one by one rather than `-string`, so that the enclosing FAST template (a string) and a binding's `string.quoted.html` value both stay open for nesting.
injectionSelector: L:source.ts -comment -string, L:source.tsx -comment -string, L:source.js -comment -string, L:source.jsx -comment -string, L:string.template.fast-element.ts meta.embedded.line.ts -comment -string.quoted.single.ts -string.quoted.double.ts -string.template.ts -string.regexp
